Fleet Doctrine

Unlocks the Fleet Doctrine decision: learn how your crews fight. Plunder, raiding or slaving, or the doctrine of your own people: broadsides for Sartosa and Araby, Ramming Speed for the freebootaz, the Drowned Dead for the Vampire Coast, slave galleys for the Druchii.
Set Out

Unlocks the Set Out decision: put to sea for three to six months on a heading of your choice. Every sea has its own prizes, monsters, navies and wonders, and the sea's mood decides much of what you meet.
Set Out
Put to sea for a season of plunder. Choose a heading: your home waters or a neighbouring sea. Each sea of the world has its own prizes, monsters, navies and wonders.
You choose a heading and put to sea for three to six months.
You have not been at sea for the last five years
The [Root.GetSeaShips] are provisioned, the [Root.GetSeaCrew] sober enough to stand, and the tide turns at dawn. Your home waters are [Root.GetSeaHome]. Where away, Captain?
Set course for the Sea of Claws: Marienburg cogs, Norse longships, and ice.
Set course for the Great Western Ocean: Bretonnian coasts and the Mists of Albion.
Set course for the Tilean Sea: Sartosa, Tilean gold and the Pirate Coast.
Set course for the waters of Araby: spice dhows and the Sultan's war-galleys.
Set course for the Southern Sea: ivory, gems and long, dead calms.
Set course for the Lustrian seas: temple gold, sea serpents and the Vampire Coast.
Set course for the seas of Naggaroth: Black Arks, icebergs and slave markets.
Set course for the Inner Sea of Ulthuan: elven treasure and the Shifting Isles.
Set course for the Far Eastern seas: jade, junks and typhoons.
Set course for the Sea of Chaos: daemon ships and warp storms.
Set course for the Inner Ocean of the Under-Empire: warpstone and darkness.

A scrawny ship's cat has come aboard with the stores and made itself at home on the cable tier. The old hands swear a fed cat keeps [Root.GetSeaPower] in good temper. The boatswain swears it ate his supper.
Feed the beast. It is a good omen.
Over the side with it.

For three days a great white albatross has followed the ship, riding the wind off the stern. The [Root.GetSeaCrew] say it carries a drowned sailor's soul and must be left alone. Your best marksman says it would make a fine shot.
Let it fly.
Take the shot.
Before the tide turns, a holy one of your own people comes down the quay asking for passage: one who knows the ways of [Root.GetSeaPower]. Turning such a passenger away is thought very bad luck.
Welcome aboard.
There is no room.

The [Root.GetSeaCrew] have a petition: they want your ship renamed after your last great deed, so every port will know who comes. The oldest sailor aboard spits over the rail. Everyone knows a renamed ship is an unlucky ship.
Paint the new name on.
She keeps her old name.
On the last night ashore the [Root.GetSeaCrew] gather at the waterline and look at you. Something must go to [Root.GetSeaPower] before the voyage: gold, or blood.
Throw in a purse of gold.
Throw in a prisoner.
The sea gets nothing from me.

The [Root.GetSeaShips] limp back into harbour, barnacled and salt-white, low in the water with what is left of the plunder. In every tavern on the waterfront your [Root.GetSeaCrew] are already telling the tale, a little bigger each time.
Ashore at last.
A sail off [Root.GetSeaTheatre]! She is [Root.GetSeaPrize], wallowing low in the water and slow as a cow. Your [Root.GetSeaCrew] are already at the rail. [Root.GetSeaCry]
Board her!
Run up the colours and tell her to strike.
Take the crew for the pens.
The Code says she pays the toll and sails on.
She may get away.
The sky off [Root.GetSeaTheatre] goes the colour of a bruise. By noon the [Root.GetSeaShips] are climbing waves taller than their masts and the rigging screams in the wind.

This is no honest storm. The wind comes from every quarter at once, lightning walks on the water, and the old hands swear they hear laughter in the thunder. [Root.GetSeaPower] is angry with you, Captain, and the sea is [Root.GetSeaMood].
Lash the helm and ride it out.
Pray to [Root.GetSeaPower].
Run for the nearest shore. This voyage is over.
The voyage ends early: you sail for home.
The water off the bow boils and something comes up out of the deep: [Root.GetSeaMonster]. Its first pass takes the bowsprit. The [Root.GetSeaCrew] look at you.
Harpoons and boarding axes! We kill it!
Every sail aloft. Run!
Throw it a prisoner and sail on while it feeds.
Too long at sea, too little gold, and now the water casks taste of rot. You hear the [Root.GetSeaCrew] muttering below, and this morning someone nailed a black spot to your cabin door.
Hang the ringleaders from the yardarm.
Break open my own share and pay them.
I will fight the first mate for the ship, here and now.
Another captain crosses your bow off [Root.GetSeaTheatre], flying no flag you know, and runs out her guns to see what you will do.

A hulk comes out of the fog with weed on her hull and dead men in her rigging, and on her quarterdeck stands Luthor Harkon himself, the mad vampire admiral of the Vampire Coast, shouting orders to a crew that drowned centuries ago. He sees you, and grins with too many teeth.

A black ravenship slides out of the sun, and the sea-dragon cloak on her captain tells you who he is: Lokhir Fellheart, the Krakenlord, Druchii raider of a hundred coasts. He raises a gauntleted hand, half salute and half challenge.

Cold mist, and then a Druchii warship close enough to see her captain: Duriath Helbane, the Lord of Khand, who has bled Ulthuan's coasts for longer than your grandfather's grandfather lived. His corsairs are already at the rail.
A dragon-headed longship from Skeggi, the Norse town on the edge of Lustria, swings across your bow, and the jarl himself stands in her prow, axe on his shoulder, measuring you up.
Run out the guns!
Hail her and parley.
Give her a wide berth.
An old friend! Break out a bottle and trade the news.
A ship drifts across your course with torn sails and no one at the helm. Her decks are empty and her boats still lashed in place. Whatever happened to her crew, it happened quickly.
Board her and search the hold.
Burn her as an offering to [Root.GetSeaPower].
Leave her to the sea.
The hold is empty.
The lookout sights land where the charts show only sea: an island off [Root.GetSeaTheatre], green and empty, with a sheltered cove and fresh water. No one has a name for it.
Chart it. Someone will pay for this map.
Bury a chest of plunder here for leaner years.
Maroon the troublemakers here.
In a few years you may come back to dig it up.
Sails off the Wasteland coast: the Imperial Navy out of Dietershafen, great carracks with Sigmar's comet on their banners, and they are hunting pirates.
Longships out of Norsca, a whole raiding fleet of them, shields along their sides, and they have seen you.
A Bretonnian sea lord's galleons bear down from the coast of Lyonesse, pennants streaming, knights in full armour on their decks.
White hulls and swan-winged prows: a squadron of the Lothern Sea Guard, the finest sailors in the world, on patrol for raiders.
The black flags of Sartosa! A Pirate Prince's squadron, and they do not share their waters.
An Estalian treasure fleet's escorts, tall galleons with priests of Myrmidia at the prow, turn to bar your way.
The Sultan's war-galleys, banks of oars beating, close in under lateen sails. Araby does not love freebooters it cannot tax.
The fog thickens and the drowned fleet of the Vampire Coast comes out of it: rotting hulks crewed by the dead, cannons crusted with coral, the sea itself heaving them along.
Reed-hulled war canoes of the Lizardmen pour out of a river mouth, skinks shrieking at the paddles, a great Saurus in each prow.
Swift Amazon war canoes slip out of the mangroves, their warriors armed with strange old weapons that glow at the tips.
A Black Ark: a floating fortress of black towers and dungeons, bigger than a city, with a swarm of reaver ships around it like crows round a gibbet. The Druchii have smelled slaves.
A squadron of Cathayan war-junks, red sails ribbed like dragons' wings, and they carry cannon that fire black powder rockets.
Ships that are not ships: hulls of bone and burning sails, crewed by things that should not exist. The warp has spat out a daemon fleet.
Rat-ships of a rival clan come squealing out of a side-tunnel, warpfire throwers glowing green at their bows.
A squadron of pirate-hunters, paid by the merchant houses of a dozen ports, has found you at last.
Give battle!
Crowd on every sail and run.
Pay them off.
You may get away clean.
You put in at [Root.GetSeaPort] to take on water and unload what you can. The waterfront is noisy, crooked and very welcoming to anyone with gold to spend.
Sell the plunder.
A night to remember in the taverns.
Hire more hands.
Buy charts of the far coasts.

For days the wind has been at your back and the sea as smooth as glass. On the last night a great school of dolphins swims alongside, and the old hands say [Root.GetSeaPower] has taken a liking to you.

The sea, [Root.GetSeaMood], heaves itself up off the bow and something stands on the water: a servant of [Root.GetSeaPower], shaped of foam and green rage, whose voice is the grinding of the deep. It names a price for your ship.
Thanks be to [Root.GetSeaPower].
Pay the price.
I bow to no fish!
Karybdis, the great whirlpool of the Sea of Claws, opens off the starboard bow, and at its rim pack ice grinds like teeth. Sailors say the wreck at its heart is full of gold.
At midnight a ship crosses your bow, lit from within, her crew standing at their posts with the patience of the dead. A ghost ship of the Great Ocean, and her captain beckons you to follow.
Lights on the shore off the Pirate Coast, swinging like lanterns on a quay. Wreckers' lights, set to lure ships onto the rocks, and the wreckers will be rich.
The reefs off Araby sing at dusk. The sailors say a djinn is bound beneath them and grants a wish to any captain bold enough to sail the reef by night.
The wind dies. For weeks the Southern Sea lies flat as a mirror and the water casks run low. Far off, a smudge of smoke rises from an island no chart shows.

A song comes over the water off Lustria, sweet as honey. The crew drift towards the rail. You know the tales: the siren calls of the Vampire Coast, that drag ships onto the reefs where the drowned wait.
An iceberg looms out of a sorcerous mist off Naggaroth, and frozen in its heart, perfectly preserved, is a Druchii ravenship with her crew still at the oars.
The Shifting Isles: islands that move in the night, harbours that open and close like mouths, and somewhere among them, an elven treasure the Asur hid long ago.
A typhoon is coming out of the east, a wall of black cloud from sea to sky. Ahead of it, driven by the wind, a fleet of Cathayan junks runs for shelter, heavy with cargo.
A warp storm boils over the Sea of Chaos, and inside it the sea runs uphill. At its heart something glows: raw warpstone, falling like hail.
The cavern roof groans. Ahead, the Run narrows under a hanging mass of rock that sheds dust with every heartbeat, and beyond it lies a forgotten Dwarf vault.
Steer into it.
Give it a wide berth.
A fishing coast, lamps out, nets on the shingle, every soul asleep. Your [Root.GetSeaCrew] grin and slip the boats over the side.
Fill the pens.
Another night.
Years ago you buried a chest on a nameless island. Today you are back with a spade, a map, and a crew that wants to watch.
Dig!
Someone has already dug it up.
The map was wrong all along.

The Freigattur needs captains who know their trade, the old Sea King tells you, leaning on the gunwale of a longship drawn up on the shingle. "Do you raid fast and run, do you hold the shield-wall, or do you take the ships up the rivers where no one expects us?"
Broadsides. Every gun at once.
Ramming Speed!
The drowned dead. They never tire and never break.
The slave galleys. Hunt them down and chain them to the oars.
Raid fast and run.
The shield-wall.
Up the rivers, where no one expects us.
Refit the Flagship

Unlocks the Refit the Flagship decision: lay down the next ship in the line without waiting for the shipwrights. A first hull for 100 gold, a proper flagship for 200 gold and three deeds at sea, and a great flagship for 400 gold and six deeds. Five years between refits.
Recruit Raiders

Unlocks the Recruit Raiders decision: muster a standing band of your own people at your capital for prestige and Infamy. Corsairs and Dreadspears for the Druchii, cutlasses and pistols for Sartosa, scimitars for Araby, boyz for the freebootaz, the drowned for the Vampire Coast. Half upkeep, kept in peace, and gone when you die.
Refit the Flagship
Empty the yards and lay down the next ship in the line: a first hull, then a proper flagship, then a great one that every port on the coast will know by her sails.
Raise a Dragon-ship
Fell the tallest pines of the fjord and raise a ship worthy of the saga: first a longship of your own, then a dragon-ship, then a great dragon whose head the skalds will sing of.
Recruit Raiders
Spread the word along the waterfront: there is plunder to be had under your flag. A band of [Root.GetSeaRaiders] will muster at your capital.
Five years have passed since the last refit
Has done at least three deeds at sea
Has done at least six deeds at sea
Has no raider band in the field already
Has not mustered raiders in the last five years
A raider band of your own people musters at your capital. It costs half upkeep, stays in peace and breaks up when you die.
Raiders Mustered
A band of raiders was mustered not long ago. The waterfront needs time to forget the last lot.

The sloop came round the headland at dawn, low in the water and running hard, and my [Root.GetSeaCrew] ran her down before the sun was a hand above the sea. Her captain went over the side rather than face me. She is fast, she is sound, and she is too good to sell. A captain should have a ship that is known: a [Root.GetSeaFlagship] to fly my colours from.

The shipwright found me in the tavern, or I found him: neither of us remembers. He has a hull on his slip, a fine one, built for a patron who drowned before he could pay. 'Fifty crowns,' he says, 'and she's yours. Forty if you stand me another.' He has been drinking since noon and he will not be sober until the hull is sold. A [Root.GetSeaFlagship] of my own...

The storm drove her onto the bar beneath my walls: a big ship, bigger than anything in my harbour, with her masts gone and her hold full of sand. No one came ashore from her. The fishermen say she is cursed. The fishermen say that about everything. With enough hands and enough rope she could float again, and she would make a [Root.GetSeaFlagship] fit to be feared.
The prize is mine.
Pay the man.
Pour him another. And another.
Raise her!
The drowned will raise her for me.
I have no use for a ship.

The shipwrights came up from the yards with their caps in their hands and their plans under their arms. My ship has carried me through enough, they say, and the timber is tired. For 200 gold they will lay down a proper flagship, a [Root.GetSeaFlagship] with the guns and the hold to match my name. The old girl can become her tender.

The master shipwright has dreamed of this ship for thirty years, and now he thinks he has found the captain to build her for. For 400 gold he will empty every yard on the coast and raise a great flagship, a [Root.GetSeaFlagship] so large that rivals will strike their colours at the sight of her topsails.
Lay her keel!
She serves as she is.

The hull goes down the slip to the cheers of the waterfront and settles in the harbour as if she had always been there. She is small as flagships go, but she is mine, and every [Root.GetSeaCrew] on the coast knows which [Root.GetSeaShip] flies my colours.
The yards were emptied for her and the forests stripped for her mast. Now the new [Root.GetSeaFlagship] rides at anchor below my walls, and the old ship looks like a jolly-boat beside her.

Half the coast came to see her launched. She took the water like a falling tower, the wave of her rocked every boat in the harbour, and when she came up she was the greatest [Root.GetSeaFlagship] on any sea that I know of. Let them come against her.
Run up my colours.

Word went along the waterfront: plunder under my flag, and no questions asked. By the end of the week the quays were full of them, the [Root.GetSeaRaiders] of every tavern from here to the headland. They will sail for me, and fight for me, as long as there is gold to share and I am alive to share it.
[Root.GetSeaCry]
The Fortress of Eternal Torture

The greatest of the Black Arks, a mountain of black rock that rivals the White Tower's own Tor Koruali. Its dungeons go down further than its towers go up, and the screaming never stops. Maranith, called Caledor's Bane, has commanded it for longer than most kingdoms have stood, and his black dragon Wrath roosts on its highest spire.
The Throne of Black Tides

A wide, squat citadel ringed with slave-galleys like a spider with its young. From its throne hall Lord Venil Chillblade sends orders to every fleetmaster of the Black Ark fleets, and every fleetmaster obeys, or is replaced.
The Citadel of Drowning Screams

Its lower halls lie below the waterline, and the tide is let into the cells twice a day. Lady Drane Brackblood keeps the rolls of the Black Ark fleets here, and the fleetmasters who forget what they owe her come to learn the tide-tables by heart.
The Palace of Oblivion

Lost at sea long ago and searched for ever since: a palace of black marble and silver chains that went into the mists off the Shifting Isles and never came out. Some say it drifts still, crewed by the dead. Some say it waits for a captain worthy of it.
The Temple of Spite

A black ark crowned with a temple to Khaine, whose altar has not been dry in four thousand years. It was Athil Khairn's once, until Duriath Helbane took it from him with a single cut, and the priests did not even pause in their chanting.
The Black Serenade
Wind moans through the hollow towers of this ark night and day, a dirge that carries for leagues across the water. Sailors who hear it at night pray to every god they know. It does not help.
The Tower of Blessed Dread

A tall, narrow ark, its battlements lined with the skulls of sea-monsters. Lokhir Fellheart, the Krakenlord, has sailed it for centuries, and his reavers swear there is no coast in the world it has not darkened.
The Spire of Cold Lament
An ark of pale grey stone that sweats rime even in the southern seas. Its slave pens are so cold that the captives' breath freezes on the bars. The Druchii who crew it never seem to notice.
The Talon of Agony
A hooked spur of rock, its towers bent like a claw closing on prey. The Talon was lost when its fleetmaster turned on the Witch King, and no one in Naggarond will say what became of either.
The Harrow of the Deep

A jagged ark whose underside is a forest of iron chains and hooks, dragged along the seabed to catch whatever lives there. It came back from its last voyage empty of crew, and was laid up in the Sea of Malice to wait for a captain with a stronger stomach.
The Tower of Midnight

Hardly an ark at all: a single dark tower on a raft of rock, a border fortress that drifted out to sea when the world broke. Small as it is, it is still a castle afloat, and there are kings who would give their crowns for one.
The Bastion of Whispered Knives
A small, crooked ark riddled with secret passages. Three of its fleetmasters have died in their beds. The fourth sleeps in a different room every night, and still he does not sleep well.
The Keep of the Weeping Chain
A squat keep whose anchor chain is hung with the bones of those who failed it. In a high wind the bones knock together, and the sound has given the keep its name.
The Eyrie of Black Gulls
A sea-stack of an ark, its cliffs white with the droppings of the black gulls that follow it in clouds, feasting on what the pens throw overboard.
The Tower of Salt and Bone
A forgotten ark, crusted with salt, its towers patched with the bones of whales. It lies at anchor in a dead lagoon of the Sea of Malice, waiting for the Witch King to remember it.
The Watch of the Hag Moon
A watchtower ark sworn of old to the convents of the Hag Sorceresses. It has no fleetmaster now, and the sorceresses who keep it are said to be choosing one.
Attain a Black Ark

Unlocks the Attain a Black Ark decision: petition the Witch King for one of the arks held in reserve at Naggarond. Sixteen Black Arks sail the world's seas, small, middle and great, and every one is unique. An ark gives prestige and retinue, sails against your enemies once in every war, and fills the pens in years of war. It passes only to a Corsair heir.
Seize a Black Ark
Unlocks the Seize a Black Ark decision: challenge another Druchii captain for their ark, by storm or by gold. Once every ten years.
Attain a Black Ark
Send gold, slaves and a carefully worded letter to Naggarond. The Witch King keeps a few arks at anchor in the Sea of Malice for captains who have earned them. Perhaps he will think you one.
The Witch King answers the petition. He may grant an ark from the reserve, or keep the gifts and tell you to wait.
Seize a Black Ark
An ark belongs to whoever can hold it. Challenge [Root.GetTitledFirstName] for theirs.
You challenge the captain for their ark: by storm or by bribing the crew. The winner keeps it.
An ark waits in the Witch King's reserve

The gifts stay in Naggarond. You may petition again in five years.
The ark drifts back into the mist, and is lost to you.
The ark's host lands at the enemy port nearest their capital in one to two months, if the war still runs.

This character has lately asked the Witch King for a Black Ark.
Challenged for an Ark

Took my Black Ark

The reply came on black vellum, sealed with the Witch King's own sign. Malekith has looked on my deeds and found them sufficient. One of the arks at anchor in the Sea of Malice is mine: its towers, its pens, its corsairs and its screaming. I am to bring it back to him full.

The reply came, eventually. The gifts were received, the slaves have been put to good use, and the Witch King thanks me for my loyalty. Of the ark there was not a word. In Naggarond, silence is an answer. I am not yet enough.
The ark is mine.
I will be patient. For now.

She came out of the mist at dawn: a Black Ark, a mountain of dark stone drifting with no banners and no lights. No reaver ships circle her. No slaves wail in her pens. Whoever commanded her is dead, or worse, and the ark is waiting for someone to claim her. My [Root.GetSeaCrew] are pale, but they are watching me.
Board her. She is mine now.
Leave the cursed thing to the sea.

The ark of [From.GetTitledName] lies at anchor, guarded by corsairs who have not been paid in a month. I can take her by storm, through the sea gate at night with my best blades, or I can let gold do the work and have the gates opened from within. Either way, by morning she will fly my banner, or I will be hanging from hers.
Storm the sea gate!
Gold opens any gate.
[From.GetTitledName] came for my ark in the night, and by dawn it was theirs. My captains, my pens, my towers, all of it. I have not forgotten. I will not forget.
[From.GetTitledName] came for my ark in the night and found it held against them. Their corpses decorate the sea gate now, the ones we found, at least. The ark is mine still.
Let them come again.

A herald of Naggarond came to my hall today, dressed in black and carrying a single iron key. The Witch King has need of another fleetmaster. One of the arks in the reserve is to sail under my command, and I am to remember, every day, whose gift it is.
Kneel and accept.
The Ark Awaits

My [Root.GetSeaCrew] are at the walls and the pens are empty: the ark is ready to sail. Word is that [ark_enemy.GetTitledName] has ports enough near their capital. Send the ark, and in a month or two its host will come ashore at their door.
Send the ark!
The ark stays at anchor.

The watchtowers saw it first: a mountain of black stone on the horizon, coming on against the wind. By noon its reaver ships were on the beaches, and by evening the host of [From.GetTitledName] had come ashore. The Druchii have come for slaves.
To arms!

A Captain's Reputation

Unlocks the Reputation decision: choose what the seas whisper of you. Dread Captain, Sea Wolf, Merchant of Plunder, the Damned of the Vampire Coast, or the Sworn Admiral of your liege. Ten years between changes.
Choose a Reputation
Every captain has a name on the waterfront. Decide what yours will be.

Sea Wolf

The Damned
This captain's crews do not stay dead. After every victory the fallen of both sides get up again, and walk into the sea to join them.

The Drowned Have Risen
The dead have risen for this captain lately. It will be a while before they rise again.
Swore their fleet to me
Answered my call to war

Every tavern from here to Sartosa has a story about me, and most of them are lies. That is no matter. A captain's name is a weapon, as sharp as any cutlass, and it is time I chose which edge to sharpen. What should the seas whisper when my [Root.GetSeaShips] are sighted?
That I am the Dread Captain, and mercy is not in me.
That I am a Sea Wolf, and no prize escapes me.
That I am a Merchant of Plunder: everything has a price.
That my dead do not stay dead.
That I am [Root.GetSeaAdmiral], sworn to my liege.

The battle was over by noon. By evening the dead had begun to twitch, and by midnight they were on their feet, ours and theirs alike, shambling down to the shore in their hundreds and wading out to where my ships lay at anchor. The sea gives up its dead, and the dead serve me.
Give them cutlasses.
A rider came from my liege with a sealed letter: [From.GetTitledName] is the enemy, and the fleet is wanted. I swore my oath as [Root.GetSeaAdmiral]. The [Root.GetSeaShips] are already making sail.
The fleet sails!
Took an ark without leave

The Reavers of the Tower

The Reavers of the Tower are descended from a Black Ark captain who raided Lothern, Marienburg and L'Anguille in a single voyage and came home with the Sea Lord of Ulthuan's banner. The towers of Naggaroth still sing of it.
The Drowned Line

The Drowned Line descends from a captain of the Vampire Coast who sailed through the temple-cities of Lustria and the harbour of Bordeleaux, and made the sea itself give up its dead. Their blood runs cold and slow.
Da Big Kaptinz
Da Big Kaptinz are the get of a freeboota who smashed Remas, Luccini and Barak Varr in one long WAAAGH! across the water. Every boy on the coast knows the story, mostly wrong.
The Sons of the Sea-Wolf
The Sons of the Sea-Wolf descend from a sea-king who burned Erengrad, sacked Marienburg and rowed up the Reik to the walls of Altdorf. The skalds have not stopped singing since.
The Corsair Princes
The Corsair Princes descend from a corsair of Araby who took Bilbali, Magritta and Tobaro in a single summer and paid their ransoms into the Sultan's treasury. Or most of them.
The Blood of the Sea Lord
The Blood of the Sea Lord descends from a captain of Sartosa who plundered the great ports of Araby and the Southlands, and came home with more gold than the Princes of the city had ever seen.
§RWarhammer:§! The Legend of the Seas
Sail It
A player who sails the legendary voyage of a sea society must take their fleet to each port of the route in turn, within five years. The AI's voyage is always rolled.
Rolled
The legendary voyage of a sea society plays out in events, for players as for the AI.
Gather the Captains

Call the captains of the society together, open the casks and tell the old stories. Every deed at sea from now on will add to the society's legend, and when it is full one of us will sail the legendary voyage.
The society's legend begins. Deeds at sea add to it, and when it is full a captain of the top rank sails the legendary voyage.
You must take your fleet to each port of the route in turn, within five years. The next port is shown on your portrait.
The voyage sails on. Three raids on the ports of the route, then the sea's best.
You win, but you do not survive the winning. Your heir founds the bloodline in your name.
The legend is lost, and the society must begin it again.
We sail!
Let another chase the legend.

[sea_legend_port.GetName] lies before us, its harbour full of ships and its warehouses full of everything the world has to sell. This is the raid the songs will be about. My [Root.GetSeaCrew] are at the rails with their blades out, waiting for the word.
[sea_legend_port.GetName] flies the colours of my own realm now, and there is nothing here to raid. We take on water, the [Root.GetSeaCrew] drink the taverns dry, and the legend sails on.
[Root.GetSeaCry]
Take the ransom and sail on.
Take on water and sail on.

They were waiting for us beyond the last headland: the warships of the Empire's High Admiral, every gun run out and every deck lined with handgunners. The admiral has heard the songs too, and means to end them here. There is no going round. There is only through.

White sails on the horizon, and then the whole sea is full of them: the eagle ships of Ulthuan, led by one of the Sea Lords of Lothern in his dragon-prowed flagship. The Asur have come to settle the score. They have come to the right place.

The water boiled, and the sea dragon rose: a serpent longer than the fleet, older than the coast, with eyes like lanterns and a mouth like a sea cave. It has slept beneath these waters since before the Sundering, and our raids have woken it.

The arms came first, wrapping the bow of the nearest ship and dragging it under as if it were a toy. Then the eye opened beneath the surface, big as a city gate. The kraken of the deeps has come up to take its due from the legend.
Meet them, and make the legend!

We won. The songs will say so. My [Root.GetSeaCrew] are cheering on every deck, but I can hear them only faintly now, and the deck is cold beneath my back. Let my blood carry the legend, since I cannot.
Tell them how it ended...

The news has come by every ship in port: [From.GetTitledName] has sailed the legendary voyage, raided the great ports and beaten the sea's own champion. The taverns are full of the story, and the captains of the society drink to a new legend.
To the legend!

Five years at sea, and the legend is no closer. The [Root.GetSeaCrew] have stopped singing the old songs. The captains of the society have stopped asking. The voyage is over, and it will be some other captain's story.
The sea keeps its legends.

The captains of the Black Arks have drunk the last of the blood-wine and named me to the voyage that every Druchii corsair dreams of: [Root.GetSeaLegendRoute], the richest ports of the Asur's friends and the Asur themselves, raided one after another until the Sea Lords of Ulthuan come out to stop us. The towers of Naggaroth will remember the one who does it.

The drowned captains of the Vampire Coast have spoken, in their way, and named me to the voyage that every dead captain longs for: [Root.GetSeaLegendRoute]. Raid them all, and the sea will send its champion to stop us. The dead remember.

Da kaptinz 'ave 'ad a big meetin' and da biggest boy (me) is goin' on da big krump: [Root.GetSeaLegendRoute]. Smash 'em all, grab all da loot, an' then sumfin' REALLY big will come out of da sea to fight us. Best day ever.

The jarls of the Freigattur have feasted three nights and named me to the voyage the skalds will sing of: [Root.GetSeaLegendRoute]. Burn them all, and whatever the sea sends against us, meet it with an axe. A saga is waiting to be made.

The corsair captains of Araby have met in the shade of the harbour walls and named me to the voyage of legend: [Root.GetSeaLegendRoute], the rich ports of the infidel north. Take them all, and the sea will send its best against us. The storytellers of the souks will tell of it for a thousand nights.

The captains of Sartosa have argued for a week, fought twice and finally named me to the voyage that every pirate dreams of: [Root.GetSeaLegendRoute], the treasure ports of the south. Take them all, and the sea itself will come to stop us. Stromfels takes the weak, and the legend takes the strong.
The voyage is done, and the Asur are still counting their dead. My name will be spoken in the towers of Naggaroth for a thousand years, and my blood will carry it.
The voyage is done, and the sea has given up its champion. The dead will sing of it in the deeps, and my cold blood will carry the legend.
We dun it! Every port smashed, every bit of loot grabbed, an' da big fing from da sea is now dinner. Me boyz an' me boyz' boyz will be da biggest kaptinz on da water forever.
The voyage is done, and the skalds already argue over the verses. The gods have watched, and my blood will carry the saga to the end of the world.
The voyage is done, and the treasure-ships are low in the water. The storytellers are already at work, and my sons and daughters will be princes of the sea.
The voyage is done, the holds are full, and every tavern in Sartosa is drinking to my name. My blood will carry the legend of it as long as there are pirates on the sea.
A legend of the seas!
Your capital, or your liege's, is a port: the Freigattur are the sea-raiders of the coast
Go a-Viking
Unlocks the Go a-Viking decision: take the longships out for three to six months on the sea of your choice. Bjornlings may sail to trade instead of raid.
Longship Doctrine
Unlocks the Norse doctrines of the Warrior Training decision: the Raider, the Shield-wall, or the River Raider who rows up the Reik and the Lynsk.
Raise a Dragon-ship
Unlocks the Raise a Dragon-ship decision: from a longship of your own to a great dragon-ship, for gold and deeds at sea.
Tribute Villages

Unlocks the Tribute Villages decision: demand that a lord on the Sea of Claws pay every year to keep his coastal villages safe. The Empire has outlawed it, so an imperial lord who pays angers the Emperor.
Hall of Hulls
Your hall is built from the ships you have taken. Every three or four deeds at sea it gains a new figurehead, and with it more renown.
The Champion's Fleet
Once in a lifetime, call the tribes together for a great fleet that rows up a river to the heart of an enemy you are at war with: Altdorf, Middenheim, Marienburg, Erengrad or Praag.
Go a-Viking
The ice is off the fjords and the longships are tarred. It is time to go a-viking.
You put to sea for three to six months on the heading of your choice.
Demand Tribute
Send a man in a bearskin to [Root.GetTitledFirstName] with a simple message: pay, every year, or watch the villages burn.
The lord may pay every year while he still will, or refuse and see his villages burn.
Takes tribute from no other lord
Has not demanded tribute in the last five years
Stop Paying the Norse
Enough. Not one more coin goes north. Let them come, if they dare.
The tribute stops. The Norse will hear of it, and may come for your villages.
Send the war-arrow to every hall on the coast. The tribes will come, the fleet will sail, and the skalds will sing of the day the longships came up the river.
A great host of the tribes lands at the heart of your enemy in one to two months.
At war with the lord of Altdorf, Middenheim, Marienburg, Erengrad or Praag
The fleet lands in one to two months, if the war still runs.
Pays Tribute to the Norse
This lord pays the Norse every year to leave his coastal villages alone.
Demanded Tribute
This raider has lately demanded tribute.
Villages Burned by the Norse
The longships came, and the coastal villages here are ashes.
Dwarf Steel
Weapons bought from the dwarf sea-king of the north. They do not break.
Hall of Hulls
A hall roofed with the upturned keels of taken ships, three figureheads over the door.
Hall of Hulls
A great hall built from the timbers of taken ships, its door guarded by six figureheads.
Hall of Hulls
A hall of hulls famed along the coast, ten figureheads staring out over the harbour.
Hall of Hulls
A hall of hulls the skalds sing of, built from the wrecks of a whole navy. Fifteen figureheads stand about it like a frozen crew.
Paid tribute to the Norse
Burned my villages
Saved our sailors
Wronged our sailors
The whale takes a boat and its crew down with it.

The ice is off the fjord, and the ships are tarred and loaded. Some of the crew have sharpened their axes. Some have packed furs and amber and walrus ivory. The Bjornlings have always done both. Where the merchants of Marienburg and L'Anguille will meet a fair price, there is no need to burn anything. Unless they will not.
We go a-viking!
We go a-trading.

Halfway across the Sea of Claws, as agreed, the merchantmen are waiting: Marienburgers, a Bretonnian cog, a fat Tilean with a parrot. They have wine and wheat and good steel, and we have furs, amber and ivory. They are nervous. They have every reason to be.
An honest deal, honestly done.
The old way. Take it all.

A Marienburg convoy has hired my longships as escort as far as the Kislev coast, at a good price. On the third day the sails come over the horizon: Skaelings, by the shields. They expect us to join them. A deal is a deal, the Bjornlings say, even against other Norse. Mostly.
A deal is a deal. Shields up!
Turn on the convoy with them.

A man in a bearskin came to my hall today and would not sit. His jarl, [From.GetTitledName], has seen my coastal villages from the sea, he says, and thinks them very pretty. It would be a shame if anything happened to them. A small sum every year would make sure that nothing does.
Pay them. The villages are worth more.
Not one penny. Tell your jarl to come and get it.
[From.GetTitledName] has refused to pay. The messenger came back with his beard singed and his words still ringing: the lord bids us come and get it.
Then we will. Burn the villages!
Let them be. There are richer coasts.
The tribute from [norse_tribute_payer.GetTitledName] did not come this year. A ship came instead, with a letter: no more. They think we have forgotten the way to their villages.

The keels of the ships we took are the roof of my hall now, and the shipwrights have set the first figureheads over the door: a mermaid from a Marienburger, a gilded griffon from an imperial warship, a grinning saint from a Bretonnian cog. Men come from up and down the coast to see them.
Another figurehead goes up on the Hall of Hulls today, hauled from the sea and set beside the others. The hall grows with every ship we take, and so does my name.
Let them look upon it and despair.

The war-arrow has gone to every hall from the Skaeling coast to the ice. The tribes have come: Skaelings, Bjornlings, Sarls, Baersonlings, hundreds of ships, thousands of warriors, more than any of the old men can remember. They are waiting for my word. Up the river, to the heart of [champions_landing.GetName]!
Up the river!

They came up the river in the morning mist: longship after longship, dragon-headed, shields along their sides, so many that the river was black with them. The Norse of [From.GetTitledName] are ashore at [champions_landing.GetName]. The bells have not stopped ringing since.
Gods help us.

'Thar she blows!' The lookout's cry brings every man to the rail. A whale, a great grey bull, rolling in the swell not a bowshot off. Oil for a winter of lamps, meat for a village, bone for a hundred carvings. And a tail that can smash a longship to kindling.
Harpoons! Row!
Let him go. The sea has given enough today.

The skerry is alive with seals, thousands of them, barking and sliding on the rocks. And among them, on the highest stone, an old woman in a grey fur cloak, watching us with eyes that are far too dark and far too round. The old men in the crew make the sign against ill luck and say nothing.
Clubs out. Pelts are pelts.
Leave the seal-folk be.

A longship came out of the fog with a black sail and a bloody shield on the mast. Her captain, [sea_nemesis.GetTitledFirstName], stood in the bow and called my name across the water, and then my father's name, and then a word the skalds do not repeat. He has heard of me, it seems. He means to be the only sea-king on this coast.
The black sail again. [sea_nemesis.GetFirstName] has found me, as I knew he would, for there is not room on the sea for both of us, and both of us know it.
Ram his ship!
Another day.

Iron ships, steaming against the wind with no sail at all: the navy of a dwarf sea-king of the north, a hold of the Norse dwarfs that has kept its own fleet since before the tribes came. Their captain stands on his deck with a beard to his belt and a hand on a rune-axe, waiting to see what we are.
Trade furs for dwarf steel.
Board the stunties!

Skeggi, at last: the Norse colony on the edge of the jungle, timber halls behind a stockade of tree trunks, dragon-ships in the harbour. [sea_lord_skeggi.GetTitledName] has come down to the shore to meet us with a horn of mead and a hundred questions about home.

The skalds say Losteriksson came this way, long ago, and built a hall before he went on to found Skeggi. We found it today: a long hall of black timber, roof fallen in, vines through the walls. The hearth is still there. So is something under it.
Mead and stories!
Dig under the hearth.

The storm drove a longship onto my rocks in the night. In the morning the fishermen found her broken on the shingle, and a score of Norsemen sitting around a fire of her timbers, half-drowned, waiting to see what I will do with them.
Feed them and send them home.
Put them to work.
Hang them from the cliffs as a warning.

A ship came home today with twenty men we thought drowned. Their longship was wrecked on the coast of [From.GetTitledName], and the southerner fed them and sent them home. The north does not forget a debt.
Word has come: twenty men of ours, wrecked on the coast of [From.GetTitledName], were put in chains and set to work. The north does not forget.
Word has come: twenty men of ours, wrecked on the coast of [From.GetTitledName], were hanged from the cliffs for the gulls. The north does not forget.
Remember the name.
The Moonlit Curse
This captain kept the Lustrian temple gold. By day nothing is wrong. By moonlight their crew are bone, and so, sometimes, are they.
Charts of the Iron Fish
Charts of the deep currents and the sea-lanes, bought from a Dawi engineer who sails beneath the waves.
The Damned Captain's Oath
This captain took the oath of a ghost ship's master to set him free. Now they cannot rest, and the sea will not let them go ashore for long.
Haunted by a Draugr
A dead sea-king walks at night, looking for what was taken from his barrow.
The Blade from the Mere
A sword forged by giants before the coming of men, found hanging in a cave beneath a haunted mere. It is far too big for any warrior, and still, in the right hands, it cuts.
The Wyrm's Ring
A ring of red gold taken from a dead wyrm's hoard. It makes its wearer rich. It has also killed every one of them, and there have been a dozen.

The new cook stumped aboard at the last port: a big, smiling man with a wooden leg, a laugh for everyone and a parrot on his shoulder that swears in four languages. By the third week half the crew would die for him. Tonight the cabin boy came to me, white as a sail: the cook has a map, an old captain's buried hoard, and he and his friends mean to have it, and my ship, before we see land.
Hang him from the yardarm, parrot and all.
Share the map. There is gold enough for all of us.
A man like that is wasted as a cook. Make him my quartermaster.

The ship that hailed us had no lights, and when the moon came out from the clouds her crew were bone, every one, grinning at us across the water. Their captain told it plainly: they took the gold of a Lustrian temple, and now they cannot die, nor eat, nor feel the wind. They have found every coin but one. It is in my purse.
Give them back their coin.
What curse? Keep the gold.

Footprints on the beach of an island no chart shows, and smoke behind the trees. We found him in a stockade of driftwood: a sailor of the old Empire, marooned twenty-eight years by his count of notches on a post, with a companion from the mainland, a parrot and a kingdom of goats. He weeps at the sight of us. Then he asks whether we might like to see his goats.
Take him home. He has learned a great deal.
Leave him his kingdom.

Something rose beneath the hull at dawn: an iron fish as long as a galleon, steam pouring from her back. A hatch opened and a Dawi climbed out, a long beard tucked into his belt and a face like a grudge. He is an engineer, cast out by his guild, and he sinks warships for the grudges of his hold. He says he has no quarrel with us. Yet.
Trade for his charts of the deep currents.
Hunt the iron fish!
Let him go his way.

The captain who came aboard had a leg of whalebone and eyes like a storm. He has hunted the pale leviathan across every ocean since it took his other leg, and he has seen it again, two days west. He begged, then ordered, then threatened: join the hunt, or be counted among its friends.
To the hunt, and damn the leviathan!
Let him hunt alone.

Where the coast has sunk into the sea, a whole people lives on rafts of lashed hulls, roped together into floating towns. They fear us, and they trade with us anyway. One of them has gills behind his ears and swims like a seal, and he swears he knows where dry land still lies.
Trade for the way to dry land.
Plunder the rafts.

The ship came up against the wind, her sails in tatters and a lantern burning at her stern. Her captain has sailed these waters for three hundred years, doomed by an oath he swore to the sea, and he cannot go ashore until someone takes it from him. He holds out a hand. Behind him his crew hold out bundles of letters for wives long dead.
I will take the oath.
I will carry your letters home.
Flee!

The island was not on any chart, and now we know why. The things in the jungle walk on two legs and speak a few words, and they are not men. The sorcerer who made them lives in a white house above the beach, and he is pleased to have visitors. He wants to know whether we would like to see the operating room.
Kill the sorcerer.
Buy his creatures. They will fight.
Burn the island, all of it.

The jarl's daughter has been shut in her hall for a year by a serpent coiled round it, a great venomous thing that eats whoever comes near. Her father has promised her to the man who kills it. The old women say you must boil your breeches and your furs in tar and roll in sand, so the venom cannot bite through. The young men laugh at them. The young men are all dead.
Boil the breeches in tar!
Let someone else be eaten.

Old Halvard baited his line with the head of an ox, for a joke, and let it down into the black water. Now the line is singing, the boat is heeling over, and something vast is coming up from the bottom of the world, something that coils and coils and does not end.
Haul! All hands, haul!
Cut the line! Cut it!

In a cove of the Sea of Chaos we found the shipyard: a hull taller than a cathedral, half-built, and every plank of it held with nails pared from the hands and feet of the dead. The cultists who build it say it will sail at the end of the world, with a crew of the damned. They are nearly finished.
Burn it to the waterline!
Lay the last nail with my own hand.
Flee, and pray it never sails.

Every night for twelve years something has come out of the fen to the jarl's mead hall, and every night it has taken a warrior. The benches are half empty. The jarl drinks alone. He has offered gold and a ship to anyone who will wait for it in the dark.
I will wait for it, with my bare hands.
Burn the fen instead.

The monster's arm hangs from the rafters, and the hall feasted until dawn. But in the night something came for it: its mother, out of the mere, and she took the jarl's oldest friend down into the black water. There is a cave beneath the mere, they say, and a blade on its wall that no man could lift.
Into the mere after her!
Let the mere keep her.

Weeks of fog and wind blew us west, far past where any chart goes. Then the fog lifted, and there was a green land: forests to the sky, rivers full of fish, grapes growing wild along the shore. The old men say Losteriksson found it once, and named it, and went on south. Now we have found it again.
Mark it well. We will come back.

In the wyrm's hoard, among the gold, there is a ring of red gold that does not tarnish. The thrall who found it would not touch it. He says it has had twelve owners since the wyrm, and every one of them grew rich, and every one of them died badly.
It is mine now.
Into the sea with it.

On the headland stands a mound, and in the mound, the old men say, lies a sea-king in his ship, with all the gold he ever took. At night a light moves on the mound. The draugr does not let anyone near his treasure, and the ones who try are found in the morning, broken, with their mouths full of earth.
Open the mound and fight the draugr.
Leave him an offering, and go.
Dig quickly, and run.
